outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor formatting differences (e.g., writing “feet” vs “ft”, including ft^3/s in parentheses) would be nitpicks if the underlying values/timestamps were correct.

Critical issues: (1) The reported latest Gage height value and timestamp are contradicted by the screenshots that show the actual latest value/time in the Continuous Data tabular view. Screenshots 4/5/6 clearly show “Latest value: 2.75 ft” with Status/Approval “Provisional” at “Sep 14, 2026 04:50:00 AM EDT”. The agent instead reported Gage height as 2.58 feet at 04:45 AM EDT, which is incorrect and not the latest displayed point. (2) The reported Discharge observation (1680 cfs at 04:50 AM EDT, Provisional) has no visual evidence in any provided screenshot: screenshots show Discharge is available and sometimes marked “Graphed” (screenshots 2/7), but none show a discharge latest-value panel or discharge tabular rows with a value/timestamp/approval. Given the task requires exact latest values/timestamps “as displayed at run time,” this discharge reporting is effectively unsupported.

What was done correctly: The station name is correctly reported and is visually confirmed in screenshot 1 (“Potomac River Near Wash, DC Little Falls Pump Sta - USGS-01646500”), and the agent did operate within the Continuous Data section for the correct site.

Outcome assessment: The primary deliverable is accurate reporting of the latest Discharge and latest Gage height continuous observations (value, unit, timestamp). The agent failed this because the gage height observation is demonstrably wrong per screenshots, and the discharge observation is not evidenced as having been displayed/captured. An average user would not accept incorrect/made-up latest readings for a monitoring station, so the task is not successfully completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open the USGS monitoring-location page for site USGS-01646500 and, specifically from the Continuous Data display, report (1) the station name and (2) the latest (most recent) Discharge and Gage height observations, each with the exact value, unit, and timestamp as displayed (including any “Provisional” labeling, with no unit/timezone conversion). The user would not be flexible on wrong or unsupported values/timestamps or mixing in non-latest/daily-statistic numbers.
